why_this_tool: The interpreter with its built-in venv module and bundled pip is the lowest common denominator on every laptop, CI runner and cluster image, so hygiene learned here carries over to every higher-level tool.
alternatives: uv (one fast binary for environments, locking and builds, with a real cross-platform lock file), Poetry (its own resolver, lock file and build backend driven from pyproject.toml), conda (also manages non-Python binaries and the interpreter itself), pip-tools (compiles a fully pinned requirements file from loose inputs), versus plain Python with venv and pip, which ships with the interpreter and is the baseline all the others build on.

setup.do: Install a current Python 3 release and confirm which interpreter version your shell launches, keeping any older versions side by side.

steps.why: A fully pinned file is the simplest lock, and comparing two environments built from it is how you prove a dependency set is reproducible. Dedicated lock tools add hashes and cross-platform resolution on top of this idea.

steps.done_when: The pip list output shows your library by name and version, and importing it works from a directory outside the project.
steps.why: Shared pipeline code should be an installable distribution with declared dependencies, not a folder added to the import path by hand.

steps.why: Type hints are the contract that static checkers and linters such as mypy and ruff enforce, and the glossary defines exactly what they are and that the interpreter does not enforce them at run time.
